CLOUD INFRASTRUCTURE FOR NGOs

Discount & Credit Programs — A Step-by-Step Guide for Indian Nonprofits
Prepared for NGOs  |  August 2026

Why This Matters
Cloud infrastructure — compute, storage, security, and hosting — is often one of the largest recurring technology costs for a growing nonprofit, whether you're running a donor database, a case-management system, a public website, or data pipelines for program monitoring. Several major cloud providers offer meaningful credits, discounts, or free tiers specifically for nonprofits. This guide covers the programs that could be verified during research, how to apply, and what to watch for.

At a Glance
Provider	What's Offered	Confirmed Route to Apply
Amazon Web Services (AWS)	$1,000 promotional credit (Nonprofit Credit Program); larger cash + credit grants via AWS Imagine Grant, including a Pathfinder award up to $200K cash + $100K credit for AI projects	Apply via TechSoup (international orgs go through TechSoup Global's partner network)
Microsoft Azure	$2,000 USD/year in Azure service credits, covering the full Azure product portfolio	Apply via the Microsoft Nonprofit portal — see our separate Microsoft Nonprofit guide
Google Cloud Platform	No dedicated compute-credit program was confirmed; Google for Nonprofits only confirms Google Maps Platform credits	Register with Google for Nonprofits for Maps credits; for broader GCP needs, contact Google Cloud sales directly to ask about current nonprofit options
Cloudflare (Project Galileo)	Free security infrastructure equivalent to Cloudflare's Business plan: DDoS mitigation, WAF, CDN, SSL, Workers, Zero Trust	Apply directly via Cloudflare's contact form, or through a partner organization (e.g., EFF, Amnesty International)
Oracle NetSuite.org	Reported to offer discounted/donated NetSuite ERP licenses to eligible nonprofits	Could not be confirmed directly in this session — contact NetSuite.org or a NetSuite partner to verify current terms


Amazon Web Services (AWS)
What's Offered
•	AWS Nonprofit Credit Program — $1,000 in AWS promotional credit, intended to help nonprofits get started on cloud infrastructure without large upfront costs.
•	AWS Imagine Grant — funding, AWS credits, and technical assistance for larger or more ambitious projects; the Pathfinder award specifically supports generative AI projects with up to $200K cash plus $100K in AWS credit.
•	Amazon Research Awards — unrestricted funds and AWS credits available to academic institutions and nonprofits doing research.
•	AWS Migration Acceleration Program (MAP) — structured support for organizations migrating existing systems to AWS.
Eligibility
•	Nonprofits with recognized charitable status in their country (in the US, this maps to specific 501(c) designations; in India, the equivalent is typically a registered Trust, Society, or Section 8 Company).
•	Organizations of any annual operating budget size are eligible for the base Nonprofit Credit Program.
•	Educational institutions (schools, colleges, universities) are excluded from this program — they should look at AWS Educate instead.
How to Apply — Step by Step
1.	Gather your documents: registration certificate (Trust Deed/Society/Section 8), PAN, 12A, 80G, and NGO Darpan ID.
2.	Register your organization with TechSoup (for India, typically via techsoupasia.org), since AWS distributes this credit through TechSoup and its partner NGO network rather than a direct AWS application.
3.	Once validated, locate the AWS Nonprofit Credit Program listing through TechSoup and submit your request — one grant can be requested per fiscal year (July 1–June 30).
4.	Redeem your credit: log into your AWS account, go to Billing Dashboard → Credits, enter the promotional code TechSoup provides, complete verification, and click Redeem.
5.	For larger project funding, separately explore the AWS Imagine Grant application on AWS's own site if your project fits its focus areas.
📌 Note
Credits are typically valid for at least one year or until used up, and you can generally request one grant per fiscal year — plan your usage accordingly rather than assuming it renews automatically.

Microsoft Azure
Azure's nonprofit credit is part of the broader Microsoft Nonprofit program, which we've covered in detail in a separate guide. In short: eligible organizations get $2,000 USD per year in Azure service credits, covering the full Azure product portfolio (compute, storage, AI, data services), plus access to a free “Nonprofit Azure Onboarding Concierge” service to help with initial setup. Registration and validation happen through the same Microsoft Nonprofit portal used for Microsoft 365 and Dynamics 365 — see our Microsoft Nonprofit Stepbystep Guide for the full application walkthrough.

Google Cloud Platform
Unlike AWS and Azure, a dedicated Google Cloud compute-credit program for nonprofits could not be confirmed during research for this guide. Google for Nonprofits confirms Google Maps Platform credits as part of its standard offer bundle, but the main Google for Nonprofits product page made no mention of general-purpose Google Cloud Platform (GCP) credits.
⚠ Please verify
If your organization needs GCP compute or storage credits specifically (beyond Maps), don't assume they're bundled into Google for Nonprofits — contact Google Cloud's sales team or check cloud.google.com directly to ask whether a nonprofit-specific GCP credit program currently exists in your region.

Cloudflare — Project Galileo
Project Galileo isn't a general compute program, but it's one of the most valuable cloud-infrastructure protections available to civil-society organizations: free security services equivalent to Cloudflare's Business plan, including unmetered DDoS attack mitigation, a Web Application Firewall (WAF), CDN, SSL certificates, Cloudflare Workers, Zero Trust access controls, cache analytics, image optimization, and PCI compliance support.
Eligibility
•	The program is targeted at organizations in human rights advocacy, civil society and democracy support, journalism and media, and arts and cultural expression.
•	Cloudflare specifically looks for “vulnerable Internet properties” — organizations likely to be targeted by DDoS attacks or other cyber threats because of their public-interest work.
How to Apply
6.	Partner route: reach out to one of Cloudflare's 40+ partner organizations (examples include the Electronic Frontier Foundation, Amnesty International, and Reporters Without Borders) and ask them to sponsor your application.
7.	Direct route: complete Cloudflare's contact form, detailing your domain, your organization's mission, your nonprofit status, your public-interest activities, and the factors that make your site a target.
8.	Cloudflare keeps participating sites confidential unless you give explicit permission to disclose your participation.

Oracle NetSuite.org
NetSuite.org is Oracle's philanthropic arm, historically known for donating or discounting NetSuite's cloud ERP/CRM software to nonprofits. This session was unable to directly access NetSuite.org's program pages to confirm current terms, discount amounts, or the application process.
⚠ Please verify
Treat NetSuite.org as worth investigating separately rather than relying on this guide for specifics — contact NetSuite.org directly or search for their current nonprofit program page to confirm what's on offer today.

Quick Checklist
•	☐ Decide which need is most urgent: raw compute/storage credit (AWS, Azure), security infrastructure (Cloudflare), or ERP software (NetSuite.org)
•	☐ Register with TechSoup (techsoupasia.org for India) as the route into AWS's Nonprofit Credit Program
•	☐ Apply through the Microsoft Nonprofit portal for your $2,000/year Azure credit, if not already done
•	☐ If your organization does human rights, journalism, civil society, or arts/culture work and faces online threats, apply to Cloudflare's Project Galileo
•	☐ Confirm directly with Google Cloud sales whether any nonprofit GCP credit currently exists in your region
•	☐ Keep core documents ready for any program: registration certificate, PAN, 12A, 80G, NGO Darpan ID

GOOGLE FOR NONPROFITS

A Step-by-Step Sign-Up & Activation Guide for Indian Nonprofits
Prepared for NGOs  |  August 2026

What Is Google for Nonprofits?
Google for Nonprofits is a free program that gives eligible charitable organizations access to a bundle of Google products at no cost or at a steep discount. Once your organization is verified, you can activate any or all of the following from a single dashboard:
•	Google Ad Grants — up to $10,000/month in free Google Search advertising
•	Google Workspace for Nonprofits — Gmail, Docs, Sheets, Drive, Meet and AI tools (Business Standard, Business Plus or Enterprise editions) free or at a nonprofit discount
•	YouTube Nonprofit Program — donation features, Donate stickers, and fundraising tools on your YouTube channel
•	Google Maps Platform credits — free credits to embed maps and location tools
•	Access to Gemini, Gemini in Notebook, Google Analytics, Google Cloud and Google Labs tools for eligible organizations

📌 Before you start
Google for Nonprofits is not available to government bodies, hospitals/healthcare organizations, or schools and universities (Google for Education serves the education sector instead).

Overview: The Journey in 6 Steps
1.	Check your eligibility
2.	Gather your organization's documents
3.	Create/request your Google for Nonprofits account
4.	Complete verification (via Goodstack, Google's validation partner)
5.	Activate the individual products you want to use
6.	Stay compliant and keep your account in good standing

Step 1: Check Your Eligibility
Before applying, confirm your organization meets Google's baseline criteria:
•	You are a registered nonprofit/charitable organization in good standing in your country.
•	Your organization is not a government entity, a hospital or healthcare organization, or a school/academic institution.
•	Your country is one of the 190+ countries where Google for Nonprofits currently operates (India is included).
•	You agree to Google's Additional Terms of Service for nonprofits.

You can double-check the current criteria any time at google.com/nonprofits/eligibility before you apply, since requirements are occasionally updated.
Step 2: Gather Your Organization's Documents
Google's validation partner, Goodstack, verifies your nonprofit status before granting access. Having the following ready will speed up the process for an Indian organization:
•	Registration certificate — Trust Deed, Society Registration Certificate, or Section 8 Company incorporation certificate, as applicable
•	PAN card of the organization
•	12A registration certificate (income tax exemption for nonprofits)
•	80G certificate, if available (helps establish charitable status, though not always mandatory)
•	NGO Darpan / NITI Aayog unique ID, if your organization has one
•	FCRA registration certificate, if your organization receives foreign contributions
•	An official organization website and an email address on your own domain (e.g., name@yourngo.org) — a Gmail-only address can slow down or block verification

📌 India tip
Exact document requirements can change and are sometimes tailored to the verification partner's checks. When you reach the sign-up form, follow the specific document checklist it shows for India rather than relying solely on this list.
Step 3: Create / Request Your Google for Nonprofits Account
7.	Go to google.com/nonprofits and select “Get started.”
8.	Sign in with a Google account tied to your organization (ideally an admin email on your organization's domain, not a personal Gmail).
9.	Select India as your country/region so you see the correct eligibility rules and available products.
10.	Fill in your organization's legal name, registration number, address, mission description, and upload the supporting documents gathered in Step 2.
11.	Review and accept Google's Additional Terms of Service, then submit your request.
Step 4: Complete Verification With Goodstack
After you submit your request, Goodstack (Google's independent validation partner) reviews your organization's legal status.
•	Typical turnaround is about 2–14 working days, though it can take longer if documents are incomplete.
•	You may be contacted by email if Goodstack needs additional documents or clarification — check your inbox (and spam folder) regularly.
•	You will receive an email confirming approval or explaining why your application was not approved.

Once approved, log back in at google.com/nonprofits to reach your organization's Google for Nonprofits dashboard.
Step 5: Activate the Products You Need
Each product is activated separately from your Google for Nonprofits dashboard by choosing “Activate products” and then “Get started” on the product you want.
5a. Google Ad Grants
•	From the dashboard, select Google Ad Grants → Get started, and complete the additional application (organization details, campaign goals).
•	Your website must be high quality, secure (HTTPS), and comply with Google's website policy before Ad Grants will approve your account.
•	Once live, keep in mind ongoing program policies typically enforced by Google: a minimum 5% click-through rate, at least two ad groups per active campaign, geo-targeting on your ads, and no single-word or overly generic keywords.
•	A linked Google Analytics/conversion tracking setup is strongly recommended so Google can see your grant is driving real engagement.
5b. Google Workspace for Nonprofits
•	Choose Google Workspace for Nonprofits → Get started, then follow the prompts to either link an existing Workspace domain or set up a new one for your organization's domain (e.g., yourngo.org).
•	Depending on eligibility, you may qualify for Business Standard, Business Plus, or Enterprise editions free or at a nonprofit discount.
•	You'll need to verify domain ownership (via a DNS TXT/CNAME record) if setting up Workspace for the first time.
5c. YouTube Nonprofit Program
•	Link your organization's YouTube channel from the dashboard to unlock nonprofit features such as the Donate button/card, a video fundraising call-to-action, and volunteer/donation link stickers during live streams.
•	Your YouTube channel should be in good standing and meet YouTube's own community guidelines.
5d. Google Maps Platform Credits
•	Activate this from the dashboard to receive monthly credits you can apply toward embedding Maps, geocoding, or location features on your website or app.
Step 6: Stay Compliant and Keep Your Account Healthy
•	Log in periodically — Google may pause products (especially Ad Grants) if an account shows no activity or falls out of policy compliance.
•	Keep your organization's registration documents current in case Google or Goodstack requests re-verification.
•	Assign at least one backup admin in your organization so access isn't lost if one staff member leaves.
•	Review Google's nonprofit program policies periodically, since terms and eligibility rules are updated from time to time.
•	Use the free how-to guides and training materials available from the Google for Nonprofits dashboard to get the most out of each product.

Quick Checklist
•	☐ Confirm organization type is eligible (not government, hospital, or school)
•	☐ Collect registration certificate, PAN, 12A (and 80G/FCRA/Darpan ID if applicable)
•	☐ Set up an admin email on your organization's own domain
•	☐ Submit application at google.com/nonprofits
•	☐ Respond promptly to any Goodstack verification requests
•	☐ Activate Ad Grants, Workspace, YouTube Nonprofit Program and Maps credits as needed
•	☐ Assign a backup admin and calendar a quarterly compliance check-in

CLOUDFLARE PROJECT GALILEO

Free Security Infrastructure — A Step-by-Step Guide for Indian Nonprofits
Prepared for NGOs  |  August 2026

What Is Project Galileo?
Project Galileo is Cloudflare's programme providing free, enterprise-grade security protection to organizations doing public-interest work that makes them targets for cyberattacks. Unlike the compute-credit programmes from AWS and Azure, this is not about hosting — it is about keeping your existing website online and safe when someone tries to take it down.
Participating organizations receive protections equivalent to Cloudflare's paid Business plan, at no cost:
•	Unmetered DDoS attack mitigation — no cap on the size of attack absorbed, which is the core of the offer.
•	Web Application Firewall (WAF) — blocks common exploitation attempts against your site.
•	Content Delivery Network (CDN) — faster page loads for visitors, including those on slower connections.
•	DNS services and SSL certificates.
•	Cloudflare Workers and Zero Trust access controls.
•	Cache analytics, image optimization, and PCI compliance support.

On confidentiality
Cloudflare keeps the identity of participating sites confidential unless you give explicit permission to disclose it. For organizations working on sensitive issues, this matters — participation does not itself become public information.

Who Is Eligible
Project Galileo is deliberately narrower than a general nonprofit discount. Cloudflare targets organizations working in:
•	Human rights advocacy.
•	Civil society and democracy support.
•	Journalism and media.
•	Arts and cultural expression.

Beyond sector, Cloudflare looks for what it calls "vulnerable Internet properties that are the targets of DDoS and other cyber attacks." A strong application demonstrates three things: nonprofit status, a clear public-interest mission, and specific factors that make your organization a likely target.
Is this the right programme for you?
If your organization's work is uncontroversial and has never attracted hostile attention, Project Galileo may not be the right fit — and a standard Cloudflare free or paid plan may serve you perfectly well. This programme is designed for organizations facing genuine threat, and applications are assessed on that basis.

Overview: Two Routes to Apply
Cloudflare offers two distinct application pathways. The partner route is generally faster and carries more weight, because a known organization is vouching for you.
1.	Partner route — request sponsorship from one of Cloudflare's 40+ partner organizations.
2.	Direct route — complete Cloudflare's own contact form.

Step 1: Assess Your Fit and Prepare Your Case
Before applying either way, be ready to articulate:
•	Your organization's mission and the public-interest work it does.
•	Your nonprofit status — in India, your registration as a Trust, Society, or Section 8 Company, supported by PAN, 12A, 80G, and NGO Darpan ID where available.
•	The domain or domains you need protected.
•	Why your organization is vulnerable — past attacks, threats received, the sensitivity of your work, or the actors likely to target you. Be specific; this is the part that distinguishes a strong application.
Step 2: Option A — Apply Through a Partner Organization
3.	Identify a Cloudflare partner organization whose remit matches your work. Named examples include the Electronic Frontier Foundation, Amnesty International, and Reporters Without Borders, among 40+ partners.
4.	Contact that organization and request sponsorship for Project Galileo.
5.	Provide them with your mission, domain, and vulnerability details so they can vouch for your application.
6.	The partner refers you to Cloudflare, who complete onboarding.
📌 Note
If your organization already has a relationship with a human rights, press freedom, or civil society network, start there — an existing relationship makes sponsorship considerably easier to obtain than a cold approach.
Step 3: Option B — Apply Directly to Cloudflare
7.	Complete Cloudflare's Project Galileo contact form on their website.
8.	Detail your domain, your organization's mission, your nonprofit status, your public-interest activities, and the specific vulnerability factors you face.
9.	Submit and await Cloudflare's assessment.
Step 4: Onboard Your Domain
•	Once accepted, you will need to point your domain's nameservers to Cloudflare — this is the standard Cloudflare onboarding step and requires access to your domain registrar.
•	Plan this with whoever manages your website, as it briefly affects DNS resolution.
•	Once active, review your WAF settings and enable the protections relevant to your risk profile rather than leaving everything at default.

A Note on Alternatives
Google runs a comparable programme called Project Shield, aimed at news, human rights, and election-monitoring organizations. We were unable to verify its current terms during research for this guide, as its pages did not return readable content. If Project Galileo does not fit or your application is unsuccessful, Project Shield is the natural second avenue to investigate.

Quick Checklist
•	☐ Confirm your sector fits (human rights, civil society, journalism, arts/culture)
•	☐ Articulate clearly why your organization is a likely target
•	☐ Collect registration certificate, PAN, 12A, 80G, NGO Darpan ID
•	☐ Identify a partner organization for sponsorship, if you have an existing relationship
•	☐ Otherwise, complete Cloudflare's direct contact form
•	☐ Arrange registrar access ahead of nameserver changes
•	☐ Review WAF settings once active rather than leaving defaults

WEBSITE & DIGITAL PRESENCE

Building a Site Supporters Can Actually Find
Prepared for NGOs | August 2026

The Point of This Guide
A great many NGO websites are invisible. Not badly designed — invisible. Someone searching for exactly the service the organisation provides will never see it, because of a handful of technical decisions made early and never revisited.
This guide covers the parts that determine whether your site can be found, funded, and used: domains, hosting, search visibility, the Google Ad Grant, and accessibility. It assumes no technical background.

Your Domain
•	Prefer a domain you own outright over a free subdomain from a website builder. A free subdomain looks provisional to donors and cannot move with you if you change platforms.
•	For Indian NGOs, both .org and .in read as credible. Avoid unusual extensions, which can look less trustworthy to first-time visitors and are occasionally filtered by spam systems.
•	Register for multiple years, and set the renewal to auto-renew. Expired domains are one of the most common and most damaging avoidable failures — the site vanishes, and email attached to the domain stops working.
•	Record who holds the registrar login, and make sure at least two people can access it.

Why the domain affects your grants
Email matters here too. Several nonprofit programmes — including Google for Nonprofits and Microsoft Nonprofit — treat an email address on your own domain as a signal of legitimacy during verification. A Gmail address can slow approval.

Hosting — Which You May Already Have Free
Option	What It Gives You	Cost

Being Found: Search Visibility Basics
Search engine optimisation has a reputation for being arcane. The parts that matter most for a small NGO are not.
1. Give every page a real title
The page title appears in the browser tab, in bookmarks, in link previews when someone shares your page on WhatsApp, and — most importantly — as the clickable headline in Google results. A page titled with your platform's default is a wasted headline.
A common and costly default
This is worth checking on your own site today. Sites built from a template or an app builder frequently ship with the scaffold's default title still in place — something like "My App" or the builder's name. It is a two-minute fix that affects every search result and every shared link.
2. Write a meta description for key pages
This is the short paragraph shown beneath your title in search results. Google does not always use it, but when it does, it is your only chance to persuade someone to click. One or two clear sentences describing what the page offers.
3. Make sure your content exists in the page itself
Some modern website frameworks build the page entirely in the visitor's browser, so the file the server sends contains almost no text. Human visitors see a normal page. Search engine crawlers and link-preview bots may see an empty shell — and therefore index nothing.
•	Symptom: sharing your link in WhatsApp or Slack produces a preview with no title or description.
•	Symptom: searching a distinctive phrase from your site in Google returns nothing.
•	Fix: enable server-side rendering or pre-rendering. Most modern hosting platforms, including Netlify and Vercel, support this — it is usually a configuration change rather than a rebuild.
A thirty-second test
This is worth testing before assuming it is fine. Paste your homepage link into a WhatsApp message to yourself. If no preview card appears with your organisation's name, crawlers are probably seeing nothing either.
4. Write for the words people actually search
Organisations describe themselves in institutional language — "capacity building for marginalised communities" — while the people who need them search in plain terms. Use both. The plain phrasing is what brings people in.

Google Ad Grants provides up to $10,000 USD per month in free Google Search advertising. It is the single largest recurring benefit in the nonprofit programme, and also the one most often left unused, because it comes with real obligations.

•	A minimum 5% click-through rate — accounts that persistently fall below this risk suspension.
•	At least two ad groups per active campaign.
•	Geographic targeting on your ads.
•	No single-word or overly generic keywords.
•	Conversion tracking, so Google can see the grant produces real engagement.
An honest assessment
The grant rewards organisations that can maintain it and quietly penalises those that cannot. If nobody has two or three hours a month to review keywords and performance, an Ad Grants account will drift below the click-through threshold and be suspended.
It is worth being realistic before applying. A well-run account is transformative for reach; a neglected one produces nothing and consumes staff attention in recovering it. Consider whether a volunteer with digital marketing experience could own it.

Accessibility
For organisations serving the public, accessibility is both an ethical and a practical matter — an inaccessible site excludes exactly the supporters and beneficiaries many NGOs exist to reach.
•	Ensure sufficient contrast between text and background. Light grey text on white is the most common failure.
•	Add alternative text to images, describing what the image conveys.
•	Make sure the site can be navigated by keyboard alone, without a mouse.
•	Use real headings rather than large bold text, so screen readers can navigate structure.
•	Provide captions on video content — which also helps the substantial number of people who watch without sound.

CYBERSECURITY FOR NGOs

Protecting Your Site, Your Data, and Your Staff Accounts
Prepared for NGOs |  August 2026

Why NGOs Get Targeted
Nonprofits are attacked for three reasons, and none of them is that attackers dislike your mission. First, you hold valuable data — donor payment details, beneficiary records, sometimes sensitive information about vulnerable people. Second, you tend to have weaker defences than a comparably sized business, which makes you an efficient target. Third, if your work touches human rights, journalism, elections, or contested policy, you may attract deliberate, motivated attacks intended to silence you.
Most NGO breaches are not sophisticated. They begin with a stolen password or a convincing email. That is encouraging, because the defences against those are cheap and largely free.

The Five Things That Matter Most
If you do nothing else from this guide, do these. In rough order of how much risk they remove per hour of effort.
Priority	Action	Why It Matters Most
1	Turn on two-factor authentication everywhere	Stops the single most common attack — a stolen or guessed password — from being sufficient on its own. Free on every major platform.
2	Use a password manager across the team	Ends shared passwords, reused passwords, and passwords written on paper. Also solves handover when staff leave.
3	Remove access when people leave	Former staff and contractors retaining live access is one of the most common and most avoidable NGO vulnerabilities.
4	Train staff to recognise phishing	Most breaches begin with someone clicking something. Twenty minutes of training beats most technical controls.
5	Back up your data, and test the restore	Ransomware and accidental deletion are both survivable with a working backup. An untested backup is not a backup.

Worth noting
Notice that four of the five cost nothing. Security spending is rarely where small NGOs are weakest — practice is.

Protecting Beneficiary Data
This is where NGO security differs meaningfully from business security. A company protecting customer data faces commercial and regulatory consequences. An organisation holding records about survivors of violence, people living with stigmatised conditions, or community members in a contested political context faces the possibility that a breach causes direct harm to someone who trusted you.
Practical measures that carry most of the weight:
•	Collect less. Data you never gathered cannot leak. Review whether every field on your intake form is genuinely used.
•	Restrict access by role. Not everyone needs to see everything. Most systems support this and most organisations do not configure it.
•	Separate identifying details from case details where the work allows it.
•	Be deliberate about where data lives. A spreadsheet on a personal laptop or a WhatsApp group is not storage; it is exposure.
•	Have a plan for what happens if something leaks — who is told, in what order, and how affected people are informed.

On Indian law
India's Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 creates obligations for organisations handling personal data. Its detailed rules and enforcement have been evolving, and this guide does not attempt to summarise the current position. If you hold sensitive beneficiary data at any scale, this is worth proper legal advice rather than a checklist — and is a strong candidate for its own article in your Compliance category.


A Realistic Starting Sequence
1.	Audit who has access to what. List every system and every person with a login. This is usually the moment organisations discover a former employee still has admin rights.
2.	Enforce two-factor authentication on email first, then everything else. Email is the master key — whoever controls it can reset the rest.
3.	Adopt a password manager and migrate the team over a fortnight.
4.	Appoint a second administrator for every critical system, so no account depends on one person.
5.	Run a twenty-minute phishing awareness session. Show real examples rather than describing them abstractly.
6.	Verify your backups by actually restoring something.
7.	If your work is likely to attract hostile attention, apply to Cloudflare Project Galileo.
8.	Write down the offboarding steps so removing access becomes routine rather than remembered.

Building a Skills Plan That Survives Contact With Reality
The standard advice — conduct a training-needs assessment, build a matrix, schedule quarterly sessions — assumes an HR function that most Indian NGOs do not have. What follows is scaled for a team where everyone is already fully committed.
Step 1: Identify the Single Points of Failure
Ask one question: if this person left tomorrow, what would we be unable to do? The answers are your real training priorities. Common ones in small NGOs:
•	Only one person knows how the donor database is structured.
•	Only one person can update the website.
•	Only one person holds the admin login for the Google or Microsoft account.
•	Only one person understands the financial reporting spreadsheet.
Training a second person in each of these is worth more than broad upskilling, and takes far less time.
Step 2: Pick One Skill Per Person Per Quarter
Not a curriculum — one skill. A quarter is long enough to absorb something genuinely, and short enough that it does not drift indefinitely. Three or four skills learned properly across a year beats a dozen half-started courses.
Step 3: Attach Learning to Live Work
•	Someone learning spreadsheets should build the report your organisation actually files, not a practice exercise.
•	Someone learning the CRM should migrate one real donor segment into it.
•	Someone learning AI tools should draft this month's genuine donor update with it.
Skills learned against real work stick. Skills learned against exercises usually do not.
Step 4: Protect the Time Explicitly
Training that happens "when things are quieter" never happens. Two hours blocked in the calendar, treated as seriously as a funder meeting, is the difference between a plan and an intention.
Step 5: Write Down What Was Learned
A short internal note — how our Workspace admin is configured, how the monthly report is produced — converts individual learning into organisational knowledge. This is the step that prevents the single-point-of-failure problem recurring with the next hire.

Microsoft	Microsoft 365 Copilot at a 15% nonprofit discount ($25.50 USD per user/month, paid yearly). Copilot Studio for building AI agents.	Via the Microsoft Nonprofit portal, as an add-on to Microsoft 365
OpenAI	Discounts on ChatGPT Team and ChatGPT Enterprise plans.	Through Goodstack's nonprofit marketplace, once verified

One important distinction
The AWS Pathfinder award is in a different category entirely from the others. The rest are tools you switch on; Pathfinder is a competitive grant requiring a serious project proposal. Do not treat them as comparable.

What These Tools Are Actually Good For
The honest answer is that AI is strong at first drafts and pattern-heavy work, and weak wherever being wrong carries a cost. Applied to NGO work, that maps roughly as follows.
Genuinely useful
•	Drafting and redrafting — grant applications, donor updates, programme reports. The first draft is the expensive part; AI makes it cheap. You still write the final version.
•	Summarising long documents — funder guidelines, government circulars, meeting transcripts. Ask for the obligations and deadlines specifically, rather than a general summary.
•	Translation and simplification — turning an English policy document into plain Hindi, or a technical report into language a community meeting can follow. Have a fluent speaker review anything that goes out.
•	Reformatting and structuring — turning messy field notes into a consistent table, or a long report into slide bullets.
•	Explaining unfamiliar material — a staff member encountering FCRA rules or a cloud billing dashboard for the first time can ask questions without needing a colleague's time.
Use with real caution
•	Anything factual that goes out unchecked. These systems produce confident, plausible, wrong answers — including invented statistics, citations, and legal provisions. Every fact in a published document needs a human source.
•	Beneficiary data. Do not paste names, health details, case notes, or anything identifying into a consumer AI tool. Enterprise and Team plans generally offer stronger data handling than free consumer tiers — check the specific terms of the plan you hold.
•	Decisions about people. Selecting beneficiaries, assessing need, or screening job applicants with AI introduces bias that is difficult to see and harder to justify to a funder or a community.
•	Financial or legal filings. A hallucinated section number in an FCRA return is your organisation's problem, not the model's.

A rule of thumb
A practical rule that holds up well: use AI freely for work you were going to check anyway, and avoid it for work you would be tempted not to check.

1.	Check what you already have. If you are registered with Google for Nonprofits, Gemini is likely already available to your staff. This costs nothing to confirm and may end the search.
2.	Pick one workflow, not ten. Choose a task your team does weekly and dislikes — drafting the monthly donor update, summarising field reports — and try AI on that alone for a month.
3.	Set a data rule before you start. Write down, in one sentence, what staff may and may not paste into these tools. Circulate it. This is far easier to establish at the outset than to retrofit.
4.	Take the free training. Google publishes three short courses aimed specifically at nonprofits: Daily Wins with AI for Nonprofits, Optimize Creativity and Fundraising with AI, and Build Smarter Workflows with AI. These are available without a Google for Nonprofits account.
5.	Review after a month. Did it save time, or move time around? Be willing to conclude that a tool is not worth its subscription.

What Is the Impact Access Program?
Twilio.org is Twilio's social impact arm. Its Impact Access Program gives eligible organizations credits and discounts on Twilio's communication APIs — the infrastructure behind SMS, voice calls, WhatsApp messaging, and chatbots. For nonprofits running helplines, sending beneficiary alerts, or doing SMS-based outreach in the field, this is often more directly useful than raw compute credit.
•	$100 one-time product credit for eligible organizations — Twilio describes this as equivalent to thousands of complimentary text messages or voice calls.

•	Ongoing discounts on a wide range of Twilio products beyond the initial credit.
•	No monthly contract requirement — you are not locked into a subscription to use the credit.
•	Access to an education hub with webinars, e-books, and sample code, plus a partner network for implementation help.

Scale of the programme
Twilio.org reports having provided $66M+ in grants, product credits, and discounts across 2025, with $224,000 specifically in product credits to social impact organizations. The $100 starter credit is the accessible entry point; larger support is negotiated separately through their sales team.

Twilio's own framing of common nonprofit use cases is worth reading as a prompt for what your organization might do:
•	Alerts and notifications — reminding beneficiaries of appointments, deadlines, or entitlements by SMS.
•	Hotlines and helplines — routing inbound calls to trained staff or volunteers, including anonymously.
•	User authentication — verifying identities by SMS where beneficiaries lack email access.
•	Marketing and fundraising — donor outreach and campaign messaging.
•	WhatsApp-based programme delivery, which is particularly relevant given WhatsApp's reach across India.

MONITORING, EVALUATION & DATA

Turning Field Records Into Reports Funders Trust
Prepared for NGOs  |  August 2026

Scope and Honesty About This Guide
Monitoring and evaluation is a professional discipline with its own literature, and this guide does not attempt to teach it. What it covers is narrower and more practical: the tools available to Indian NGOs at nonprofit rates, and the data habits that determine whether those tools produce anything useful.
⚠ What could not be verified
Several specialist M&E platforms commonly used by NGOs — including KoboToolbox and Power BI's nonprofit pricing — could not be verified against their own live pages during research for this guide. Where a tool's terms are unconfirmed, this document says so rather than stating figures. Confirm pricing and eligibility directly before committing.

Start With the Question, Not the Tool
The most common failure in NGO data work is not choosing the wrong software. It is collecting a great deal of data that answers no particular question, and then being unable to say anything confident when a funder asks about outcomes.
Before selecting any tool, write down the handful of questions your organisation genuinely needs to answer:
•	How many people did we reach, and how confident are we in that number?
•	Did the thing we set out to change actually change?
•	Which parts of the programme work better than others, and where?
•	What do we need to report to this specific funder, in what format, by when?
Every field you collect should trace back to one of these. Fields that trace to nothing are pure cost — staff time to gather, storage risk to hold, and noise when analysing.

A link worth making
This connects directly to data protection. Every unnecessary field about a beneficiary is data you must secure and could one day leak. Collecting less is both better practice and less risk.


Tools You Can Confirm Access To
The following are confirmed from the providers' own nonprofit pages:
Tool	Nonprofit Terms	Useful For
Microsoft Power Apps	Free for up to 10 users, then $2.50 USD per user/month	Building a custom low-code data collection or case management app
Microsoft Power Automate	$3.75 USD per user/month, paid yearly	Automating repetitive steps — moving form responses into a sheet, sending reminders
Google Analytics	Included with Google for Nonprofits	Understanding website and campaign reach
Google Cloud / Azure / AWS	Credits covered in the Cloud Infrastructure guides	Hosting a database when spreadsheets stop coping
Microsoft Copilot Studio	Available through the nonprofit portal	Building AI agents over your own data — check pricing, not published

Tools Worth Investigating, Terms Unconfirmed
•	KoboToolbox — widely used for offline-capable mobile data collection in humanitarian and development work. Its free tier and nonprofit terms could not be confirmed here; check kobotoolbox.org directly.
•	Power BI — Microsoft's dashboarding tool. It was not listed on the Microsoft nonprofit pages reviewed, so whether nonprofit pricing exists separately from Microsoft 365 licensing needs checking.
•	Looker Studio — Google's free dashboard tool, which connects to Google Sheets and Analytics. Generally free to use, though its position within the Google for Nonprofits bundle was not confirmed.


The Habits That Matter More Than the Software
1. Decide your definitions before you collect
What counts as a "beneficiary reached"? Someone who attended once, or completed a programme? Organisations frequently discover mid-year that two field teams have been counting differently, which makes the aggregate meaningless. Write the definitions down and share them.
2. Collect once, use many times
If field staff fill one form for internal records, another for a funder, and a third for the annual report, the data will diverge and morale will suffer. Design one collection process, then produce different views from it.
3. Keep raw data separate from analysis
Never edit your original records to produce a chart. Keep the raw collected data untouched, and do calculations in a separate sheet or layer. When a funder queries a number a year later, you need to be able to trace it back.
4. Timestamp and attribute everything
Every record should carry when it was collected and by whom. This is what makes it possible to investigate anomalies rather than simply distrusting the whole dataset.
5. Plan for poor connectivity
Field data collection in much of India cannot assume a reliable connection. Tools that work offline and sync later are not a luxury; choosing a connection-dependent tool is a decision to lose data.

Reporting: Making the Numbers Legible
Analysis that nobody reads has no value. A few principles that hold up well:
•	Lead with the finding, not the methodology. Funders read the first line; the method belongs in an annexe.
•	Use simple chart types. A bar chart understood immediately beats a sophisticated visualisation that requires explanation.
•	Show change over time where you have it — a single snapshot rarely demonstrates impact.
•	Be honest about what the data cannot show. Funders trust organisations that state limitations more than those that claim certainty they cannot have.
•	Keep a consistent format between reporting periods, so readers can compare.

A suggested follow-up article
If your Knowledge Hub adds a data visualisation article later, the failure modes are worth covering specifically — truncated axes, pie charts with too many segments, and percentages quoted without the underlying sample size are the three that most often mislead funders unintentionally.

Quick Checklist
•	☐ Write down the four or five questions your data must answer
•	☐ Remove collection fields that do not serve one of them
•	☐ Agree and document your definitions across all field teams
•	☐ Check whether Power Apps' free tier for 10 users covers your needs
•	☐ Verify KoboToolbox's current terms directly if you need offline collection
•	☐ Keep raw data separate from analysis, permanently
•	☐ Ensure every record carries a timestamp and a collector
•	☐ Choose tools that work offline if fieldwork demands it

Google for Nonprofits — Products (Analytics, Cloud)

KoboToolbox, Power BI nonprofit pricing, and Looker Studio's inclusion in the Google bundle are all unconfirmed and flagged as such above. The data practice guidance reflects established professional practice rather than a cited source.

## फील्ड रिकॉर्ड को ऐसी रिपोर्ट में बदलना जिस पर फंडर भरोसा करें

**NGOs के लिए तैयार | अगस्त 2026**

### इस गाइड का दायरा और ईमानदारी

निगरानी और मूल्यांकन (Monitoring & Evaluation — M&E) अपने अलग साहित्य और पेशेवर मानकों वाला एक विशिष्ट क्षेत्र है, और यह गाइड इसे सिखाने का प्रयास नहीं करती। इसका दायरा अधिक सीमित और व्यावहारिक है: भारतीय NGOs के लिए गैर-लाभकारी दरों पर उपलब्ध टूल्स और वे डेटा संबंधी आदतें, जो यह तय करती हैं कि इन टूल्स से वास्तव में कोई उपयोगी परिणाम मिलता है या नहीं।

### ⚠ जिन चीज़ों की पुष्टि नहीं हो सकी

NGOs द्वारा व्यापक रूप से उपयोग किए जाने वाले कुछ विशेषज्ञ M&E प्लेटफॉर्म — जिनमें KoboToolbox और Power BI की nonprofit pricing शामिल है — इस गाइड के शोध के दौरान उनके आधिकारिक लाइव पेजों से सत्यापित नहीं किए जा सके। जहां किसी टूल की शर्तें पुष्ट नहीं हैं, वहां यह दस्तावेज़ आंकड़े बताने के बजाय स्पष्ट रूप से ऐसा कहता है। किसी भी टूल को अपनाने से पहले उसकी कीमत और पात्रता सीधे प्रदाता से सत्यापित करें।

## टूल से नहीं, सवाल से शुरुआत करें

NGO डेटा कार्य में सबसे आम समस्या गलत सॉफ्टवेयर चुनना नहीं है। समस्या यह है कि बहुत सारा ऐसा डेटा एकत्र कर लिया जाता है जो किसी विशेष सवाल का जवाब नहीं देता। फिर जब कोई फंडर कार्यक्रम के परिणामों के बारे में पूछता है, तो संगठन आत्मविश्वास से कुछ कह नहीं पाता।

किसी भी टूल का चयन करने से पहले उन कुछ महत्वपूर्ण सवालों को लिखें जिनका आपकी संस्था को वास्तव में जवाब देना है:

* हमने कितने लोगों तक पहुंच बनाई, और हमें इस संख्या पर कितना भरोसा है?
* जिस बदलाव को लाने के लिए हमने काम शुरू किया था, क्या वास्तव में वह बदलाव आया?
* कार्यक्रम के कौन से हिस्से दूसरों की तुलना में बेहतर काम कर रहे हैं और कहां?
* इस विशेष फंडर को हमें क्या रिपोर्ट करना है, किस प्रारूप में और कब तक?

आप जो भी फील्ड डेटा एकत्र करते हैं, उसका संबंध इनमें से किसी एक सवाल से होना चाहिए। जिन फील्ड्स का किसी सवाल से संबंध नहीं है, वे केवल अतिरिक्त लागत हैं — उन्हें एकत्र करने में कर्मचारियों का समय, उन्हें सुरक्षित रखने में स्टोरेज जोखिम और विश्लेषण के दौरान अनावश्यक शोर।

### एक महत्वपूर्ण संबंध

इसका सीधा संबंध डेटा सुरक्षा से है। किसी लाभार्थी के बारे में अनावश्यक रूप से एकत्र किया गया हर फील्ड ऐसा डेटा है जिसे आपको सुरक्षित रखना होगा और जो भविष्य में लीक हो सकता है। कम डेटा एकत्र करना बेहतर प्रक्रिया भी है और कम जोखिम भी।

## ऐसे टूल्स जिनकी जांच करना उचित है, लेकिन शर्तों की पुष्टि नहीं हुई है

## वे आदतें जो सॉफ्टवेयर से अधिक महत्वपूर्ण हैं

### 1. डेटा एकत्र करने से पहले अपनी परिभाषाएं तय करें

"लाभार्थी तक पहुंच" से आपका क्या मतलब है? कोई व्यक्ति जो केवल एक बार कार्यक्रम में शामिल हुआ, या जिसने पूरा कार्यक्रम पूरा किया?

अक्सर संगठनों को वर्ष के बीच में पता चलता है कि दो field teams अलग-अलग तरीके से गिनती कर रही हैं, जिससे कुल आंकड़ा अर्थहीन हो जाता है। परिभाषाएं लिखित रूप में तय करें और सभी टीमों के साथ साझा करें।

### 2. एक बार डेटा एकत्र करें, कई बार उपयोग करें

यदि field staff आंतरिक रिकॉर्ड के लिए एक फॉर्म, फंडर के लिए दूसरा और annual report के लिए तीसरा फॉर्म भरते हैं, तो डेटा अलग-अलग हो जाएगा और कर्मचारियों का मनोबल भी प्रभावित होगा। एक ही collection process तैयार करें और उसी से अलग-अलग views तैयार करें।

### 3. Raw data को analysis से अलग रखें

चार्ट बनाने के लिए अपने मूल रिकॉर्ड को कभी edit न करें। एकत्र किया गया raw data अपरिवर्तित रखें और calculations किसी अलग sheet या layer में करें। यदि कोई फंडर एक साल बाद किसी संख्या पर सवाल उठाता है, तो आपको उस संख्या को मूल रिकॉर्ड तक वापस trace करने में सक्षम होना चाहिए।

### 4. हर चीज़ पर timestamp और attribution रखें

हर रिकॉर्ड में यह जानकारी होनी चाहिए कि उसे कब और किसने एकत्र किया। इससे anomalies की जांच करना संभव होता है, बजाय इसके कि पूरे dataset पर ही अविश्वास किया जाए।

### 5. खराब connectivity के लिए योजना बनाएं

भारत के कई हिस्सों में field data collection के दौरान reliable internet connection की गारंटी नहीं दी जा सकती। ऐसे टूल्स जो offline काम कर सकते हैं और बाद में sync होते हैं, कोई luxury नहीं हैं; connection-dependent tool चुनना डेटा खोने का जोखिम स्वीकार करने जैसा है।

## Reporting: आंकड़ों को समझने योग्य बनाना

जिस analysis को कोई पढ़ता ही नहीं, उसका कोई मूल्य नहीं है। कुछ सिद्धांत विशेष रूप से उपयोगी हैं:

* **Methodology से नहीं, finding से शुरुआत करें।** Funders पहली लाइन पढ़ते हैं; methodology को annexure में रखा जा सकता है।
* **सरल chart types का उपयोग करें।** ऐसा bar chart जिसे तुरंत समझा जा सके, उस sophisticated visualisation से बेहतर है जिसे समझाने की आवश्यकता पड़े।
* **जहां संभव हो, समय के साथ बदलाव दिखाएं।** केवल एक snapshot आमतौर पर impact साबित करने के लिए पर्याप्त नहीं होता।
* **डेटा क्या नहीं दिखा सकता, इसके बारे में ईमानदार रहें।** Funders उन संगठनों पर अधिक भरोसा करते हैं जो अपनी limitations बताते हैं, बजाय उन संगठनों के जो ऐसी certainty का दावा करते हैं जिसे डेटा समर्थन नहीं करता।
* **Reporting periods के बीच consistent format रखें**, ताकि पाठक तुलना कर सकें।

## सुझाया गया follow-up article

यदि आपका Knowledge Hub बाद में data visualisation पर कोई article जोड़ता है, तो उसमें विशेष रूप से उन failure modes को शामिल करना उपयोगी होगा जो अक्सर funders को अनजाने में गुमराह करते हैं — truncated axes, बहुत अधिक segments वाले pie charts और underlying sample size बताए बिना percentages का उल्लेख।

## फील्ड रेकॉर्ड्सचे फंडर्सचा विश्वास संपादन करणाऱ्या अहवालांमध्ये रूपांतर

### या मार्गदर्शकाचा आवाका आणि या संदर्भातील स्पष्टता

Monitoring and Evaluation (M&E) हे स्वतःच्या व्यावसायिक साहित्य आणि मानकांसह एक स्वतंत्र क्षेत्र आहे आणि हे मार्गदर्शक ते शिकवण्याचा प्रयत्न करत नाही. याचा आवाका अधिक मर्यादित आणि व्यावहारिक आहे: भारतीय NGOs साठी nonprofit दरांमध्ये उपलब्ध असलेली साधने आणि या साधनांमधून प्रत्यक्षात उपयुक्त परिणाम मिळतील की नाही हे ठरवणाऱ्या डेटा-सवयी.

### ⚠ ज्या गोष्टींची पडताळणी करता आली नाही

NGOs मध्ये मोठ्या प्रमाणावर वापरली जाणारी काही विशेषज्ञ M&E प्लॅटफॉर्म्स — ज्यामध्ये KoboToolbox आणि Power BI ची nonprofit pricing यांचा समावेश आहे — या मार्गदर्शकासाठी केलेल्या संशोधनादरम्यान त्यांच्या अधिकृत live pages वरून सत्यापित करता आली नाहीत. एखाद्या साधनाच्या अटींची खात्री नसल्यास हा दस्तऐवज आकडे सांगण्याऐवजी ते स्पष्टपणे नमूद करतो. कोणतेही साधन स्वीकारण्यापूर्वी त्याची किंमत आणि पात्रता थेट प्रदात्याकडून तपासा.

## साधनापासून नव्हे, तर प्रश्नापासून सुरुवात करा

NGO डेटा कार्यातील सर्वात सामान्य अपयश म्हणजे चुकीचे software निवडणे नव्हे. समस्या अशी असते की कोणत्याही विशिष्ट प्रश्नाचे उत्तर न देणारा मोठ्या प्रमाणात डेटा गोळा केला जातो आणि नंतर funder ने परिणामांबद्दल विचारल्यावर आत्मविश्वासाने काही सांगता येत नाही.

कोणतेही साधन निवडण्यापूर्वी आपल्या संस्थेला खरोखर उत्तर द्यायचे असलेले काही महत्त्वाचे प्रश्न लिहून ठेवा:

* आम्ही किती लोकांपर्यंत पोहोचलो आणि त्या संख्येबद्दल आम्हाला किती खात्री आहे?
* आम्ही बदल घडवून आणण्यासाठी जे ठरवले होते, तो बदल प्रत्यक्षात झाला का?
* कार्यक्रमाचे कोणते भाग इतरांपेक्षा चांगले काम करत आहेत आणि कुठे?
* या विशिष्ट funder ला आम्ही काय अहवाल द्यायचा आहे, कोणत्या स्वरूपात आणि केव्हा?

तुम्ही गोळा करत असलेल्या प्रत्येक field चा संबंध यापैकी एका प्रश्नाशी असला पाहिजे. कोणत्याही प्रश्नाशी संबंध नसलेले fields म्हणजे निव्वळ खर्च — ते गोळा करण्यासाठी कर्मचाऱ्यांचा वेळ, साठवण्यासाठी storage risk आणि analysis करताना निर्माण होणारा अनावश्यक noise.

### एक महत्त्वाचा संबंध

याचा थेट संबंध data protection शी आहे. लाभार्थ्याबद्दल अनावश्यकपणे गोळा केलेला प्रत्येक field म्हणजे तुम्हाला सुरक्षित ठेवावा लागणारा डेटा आणि भविष्यात कधीतरी leak होऊ शकणारी माहिती. कमी डेटा गोळा करणे ही चांगली पद्धतही आहे आणि कमी जोखमीची पद्धतही.

## Software पेक्षा अधिक महत्त्वाच्या सवयी

### 1. डेटा गोळा करण्यापूर्वी व्याख्या निश्चित करा

"Beneficiary reached" म्हणजे नेमके काय? एखादी व्यक्ती एकदा कार्यक्रमाला उपस्थित राहिली, की तिने पूर्ण programme पूर्ण केले?

संस्थांना अनेकदा वर्षाच्या मध्यावर लक्षात येते की दोन field teams वेगवेगळ्या पद्धतीने मोजणी करत आहेत, ज्यामुळे एकत्रित आकडा अर्थहीन होतो. व्याख्या लिहून ठेवा आणि सर्व टीम्ससोबत share करा.

### 2. एकदा गोळा करा, अनेकदा वापरा

Field staff ने internal records साठी एक form, funder साठी दुसरा आणि annual report साठी तिसरा form भरला, तर डेटा वेगवेगळा होईल आणि morale वरही परिणाम होईल. एक collection process तयार करा आणि त्यातून वेगवेगळी views तयार करा.

### 3. Raw data आणि analysis वेगळे ठेवा

Chart तयार करण्यासाठी मूळ records कधीही edit करू नका. गोळा केलेला raw data अपरिवर्तित ठेवा आणि calculations वेगळ्या sheet किंवा layer मध्ये करा. Funder ने एका वर्षानंतर एखाद्या आकड्याबद्दल प्रश्न विचारला, तर तो आकडा मूळ नोंदीपर्यंत trace करता आला पाहिजे.

### 4. प्रत्येक गोष्टीला timestamp आणि attribution द्या

प्रत्येक record मध्ये तो केव्हा आणि कोणी गोळा केला हे असले पाहिजे. त्यामुळे anomalies ची चौकशी करता येते, संपूर्ण dataset वरच अविश्वास ठेवण्याची गरज पडत नाही.

### 5. खराब connectivity साठी नियोजन करा

भारताच्या अनेक भागांत field data collection करताना reliable internet connection गृहीत धरता येत नाही. Offline काम करणारी आणि नंतर sync होणारी साधने luxury नाहीत; connection-dependent tool निवडणे म्हणजे डेटा गमावण्याचा धोका स्वीकारणे.

## Reporting: आकडे समजण्यास सुलभ करणे

कोणीही वाचत नसलेल्या analysis चे कोणतेही मूल्य नाही. काही तत्त्वे विशेषतः उपयुक्त आहेत:

* **Methodology पेक्षा finding ने सुरुवात करा.** Funders पहिली ओळ वाचतात; method annexe मध्ये ठेवता येतो.

* **Reporting periods मध्ये consistent format ठेवा**, जेणेकरून वाचक तुलना करू शकतील.

## களப் பதிவுகளை நிதியளிப்பாளர்கள் நம்பும் அறிக்கைகளாக மாற்றுதல்

**NGO-களுக்காக தயாரிக்கப்பட்டது | ஆகஸ்ட் 2026**

### இந்த வழிகாட்டியின் வரம்பும் நேர்மையான விளக்கமும்

Monitoring and Evaluation (M&E) என்பது தனக்கென தனித்துவமான தொழில்முறை இலக்கியமும் தரநிலைகளும் கொண்ட ஒரு துறையாகும். இந்த வழிகாட்டி அந்தத் துறையை கற்றுக்கொடுப்பதை நோக்கமாகக் கொண்டதல்ல. இதன் நோக்கம் மிகவும் குறுகியதும் நடைமுறைக்குரியதுமாகும்: இந்திய NGO-களுக்கு nonprofit விகிதங்களில் கிடைக்கும் கருவிகள் மற்றும் அந்தக் கருவிகள் உண்மையில் பயனுள்ள முடிவுகளை வழங்குமா என்பதை தீர்மானிக்கும் தரவு தொடர்பான பழக்கவழக்கங்கள்.

### ⚠ சரிபார்க்க முடியாதவை

NGO-களால் பரவலாகப் பயன்படுத்தப்படும் சில சிறப்பு M&E தளங்கள் — KoboToolbox மற்றும் Power BI-யின் nonprofit pricing உட்பட — இந்த வழிகாட்டிக்கான ஆய்வின்போது அவற்றின் சொந்த அதிகாரப்பூர்வ live pages மூலம் சரிபார்க்க முடியவில்லை. ஒரு கருவியின் விதிமுறைகள் உறுதிப்படுத்தப்படாத இடங்களில், இந்த ஆவணம் எண்ணிக்கைகளை கூறுவதற்குப் பதிலாக அதைத் தெளிவாகக் குறிப்பிடுகிறது. எந்தக் கருவியையும் தேர்வு செய்வதற்கு முன் அதன் விலை மற்றும் தகுதியை நேரடியாக வழங்குநரிடம் உறுதிப்படுத்துங்கள்.

## கருவியிலிருந்து அல்ல, கேள்வியிலிருந்து தொடங்குங்கள்

NGO தரவுப் பணியில் மிகவும் பொதுவான தோல்வி தவறான software-ஐத் தேர்வு செய்வது அல்ல. எந்த ஒரு குறிப்பிட்ட கேள்விக்கும் பதிலளிக்காத அளவுக்கு அதிகமான தரவைச் சேகரிப்பதே பிரச்சினை. பின்னர் ஒரு funder முடிவுகளைப் பற்றி கேட்கும்போது, நம்பிக்கையுடன் எதையும் கூற முடியாமல் போகிறது.

எந்தக் கருவியையும் தேர்வு செய்வதற்கு முன், உங்கள் நிறுவனம் உண்மையில் பதிலளிக்க வேண்டிய முக்கியமான சில கேள்விகளை எழுதுங்கள்:

* நாங்கள் எத்தனை பேரைச் சென்றடைந்தோம், அந்த எண்ணிக்கையில் எவ்வளவு நம்பிக்கை உள்ளது?
* நாம் மாற்றத்தை ஏற்படுத்த வேண்டும் என்று திட்டமிட்டது உண்மையில் மாற்றமடைந்ததா?
* திட்டத்தின் எந்தப் பகுதிகள் மற்றவற்றை விட சிறப்பாக செயல்படுகின்றன, எங்கு?
* இந்த குறிப்பிட்ட funder-க்கு நாம் என்ன அறிக்கை சமர்ப்பிக்க வேண்டும், எந்த வடிவத்தில், எப்போது?

நீங்கள் சேகரிக்கும் ஒவ்வொரு field-உம் இவற்றில் ஏதேனும் ஒரு கேள்வியுடன் தொடர்புடையதாக இருக்க வேண்டும். எந்தக் கேள்வியுடனும் தொடர்பில்லாத fields அனைத்தும் கூடுதல் செலவாகும் — அவற்றைச் சேகரிக்க ஊழியர்களின் நேரம், சேமிக்க storage risk மற்றும் analysis செய்யும்போது தேவையற்ற noise.

### ஒரு முக்கியமான தொடர்பு

இது data protection உடன் நேரடியாக தொடர்புடையது. ஒரு beneficiary பற்றிய தேவையற்ற ஒவ்வொரு field-உம் நீங்கள் பாதுகாக்க வேண்டிய தரவாகும்; அது ஒருநாள் கசிந்து விடக்கூடிய அபாயமும் உள்ளது. குறைவான தரவைச் சேகரிப்பது சிறந்த நடைமுறையும் குறைந்த அபாயமும் ஆகும்.

## Software-ஐ விட முக்கியமான பழக்கங்கள்

### 1. தரவைச் சேகரிப்பதற்கு முன் உங்கள் வரையறைகளைத் தீர்மானியுங்கள்

"Beneficiary reached" என்றால் என்ன? ஒருமுறை நிகழ்ச்சியில் கலந்து கொண்டவரா, அல்லது முழுத் திட்டத்தையும் முடித்தவரா?

பல நிறுவனங்கள் ஆண்டின் நடுப்பகுதியில் இரண்டு field teams வெவ்வேறு முறையில் எண்ணிக்கை செய்திருப்பதை கண்டறிகின்றன. இதனால் மொத்தத் தரவு அர்த்தமற்றதாகிறது. வரையறைகளை எழுதிப் பதிவு செய்து, அனைத்து குழுக்களுடனும் பகிருங்கள்.

### 2. ஒருமுறை சேகரித்து, பலமுறை பயன்படுத்துங்கள்

Field staff internal records-க்கு ஒரு form, funder-க்கு மற்றொரு form, annual report-க்கு மூன்றாவது form நிரப்பினால், தரவு வேறுபடும் மற்றும் பணியாளர்களின் மனநிலையும் பாதிக்கப்படும். ஒரே collection process-ஐ வடிவமைத்து, அதிலிருந்து பல்வேறு views-ஐ உருவாக்குங்கள்.

### 3. Raw data-வை analysis-இலிருந்து தனியாக வைத்திருங்கள்

Chart உருவாக்குவதற்காக உங்கள் original records-ஐ ஒருபோதும் edit செய்யாதீர்கள். சேகரிக்கப்பட்ட raw data-வை மாற்றமின்றி வைத்திருந்து, calculations-ஐ தனி sheet அல்லது layer-ல் செய்யுங்கள். ஒரு வருடத்திற்குப் பிறகு funder ஒரு எண்ணைப் பற்றி கேள்வி எழுப்பினால், அந்த எண்ணை அதன் மூலப் பதிவுவரை trace செய்ய முடியும்.

### 4. அனைத்திற்கும் timestamp மற்றும் attribution வைத்திருங்கள்

ஒவ்வொரு record-லும் அது எப்போது மற்றும் யாரால் சேகரிக்கப்பட்டது என்பதைக் குறிப்பிட வேண்டும். இதன் மூலம் anomalies-ஐ ஆராய முடியும்; முழு dataset-ஐயே சந்தேகிக்க வேண்டிய நிலை ஏற்படாது.

### 5. மோசமான connectivity-க்குத் திட்டமிடுங்கள்

இந்தியாவின் பல பகுதிகளில் field data collection செய்யும்போது reliable internet connection இருப்பதாகக் கருத முடியாது. Offline-ல் வேலை செய்து பின்னர் sync செய்யக்கூடிய கருவிகள் luxury அல்ல; connection-dependent tool-ஐத் தேர்வு செய்வது தரவை இழக்கும் முடிவாக இருக்கலாம்.

## Reporting: எண்களைப் புரிந்துகொள்ளக்கூடியதாக மாற்றுதல்

யாரும் படிக்காத analysis-க்கு மதிப்பு இல்லை. சில அடிப்படை விதிகள் நன்றாகப் பயன்படுகின்றன:

* **Methodology-யால் அல்ல, finding-ஆல் தொடங்குங்கள்.** Funders முதல் வரியைப் படிப்பார்கள்; method-ஐ annexe-ல் வைக்கலாம்.
* **எளிய chart types-ஐப் பயன்படுத்துங்கள்.** உடனடியாகப் புரியும் bar chart, விளக்கம் தேவைப்படும் sophisticated visualisation-ஐ விட சிறந்தது.
* **காலப்போக்கில் ஏற்பட்ட மாற்றத்தை, கிடைக்கும் இடங்களில் காட்டுங்கள்.** ஒரு snapshot மட்டும் impact-ஐ நிரூபிக்க அரிதாகவே போதுமானது.
* **தரவு எதை காட்ட முடியாது என்பதில் நேர்மையாக இருங்கள்.** தரவு ஆதரிக்காத certainty-ஐக் கூறும் நிறுவனங்களை விட limitations-ஐ வெளிப்படையாகக் கூறும் நிறுவனங்களை funders அதிகம் நம்புகிறார்கள்.
* **Reporting periods-க்கு இடையில் ஒரே மாதிரியான format-ஐ வைத்திருங்கள்**, இதனால் வாசகர்கள் ஒப்பிட முடியும்.

## பரிந்துரைக்கப்படும் follow-up article

உங்கள் Knowledge Hub பின்னர் data visualisation பற்றிய article ஒன்றைச் சேர்த்தால், funders-ஐத் தவறுதலாக வழிதவறச் செய்யக்கூடிய failure modes குறித்து குறிப்பாகப் பேசுவது பயனுள்ளதாக இருக்கும் — truncated axes, அதிகமான segments கொண்ட pie charts மற்றும் underlying sample size இல்லாமல் percentages குறிப்பிடுதல் ஆகியவை மிகவும் பொதுவானவை.

## Quick Checklist

* ☐ உங்கள் தரவு பதிலளிக்க வேண்டிய நான்கு அல்லது ஐந்து கேள்விகளை எழுதுங்கள்
* ☐ அவற்றில் எந்தக் கேள்விக்கும் பயன்படாத collection fields-ஐ அகற்றுங்கள்
* ☐ அனைத்து field teams-க்கும் definitions குறித்து ஒப்புதல் பெற்று அவற்றை document செய்யுங்கள்
* ☐ Power Apps-ன் 10 users வரையிலான free tier உங்கள் தேவைகளை பூர்த்தி செய்கிறதா என்பதைச் சரிபாருங்கள்
* ☐ Offline collection தேவைப்பட்டால் KoboToolbox-ன் தற்போதைய விதிமுறைகளை நேரடியாகச் சரிபாருங்கள்
* ☐ Raw data-வை analysis-இலிருந்து நிரந்தரமாகத் தனியாக வைத்திருங்கள்
* ☐ ஒவ்வொரு record-லும் timestamp மற்றும் collector தகவல் இருப்பதை உறுதிப்படுத்துங்கள்
* ☐ Fieldwork தேவைப்பட்டால் offline-ல் இயங்கும் கருவிகளைத் தேர்வு செய்யுங்கள்

Power Apps மற்றும் Power Automate தொடர்பான எண்ணிக்கைகள் Microsoft-ன் அதிகாரப்பூர்வ பக்கத்திலிருந்து உறுதிப்படுத்தப்பட்டுள்ளன. ## ఫీల్డ్ రికార్డులను నిధుల దాతలు విశ్వసించే నివేదికలుగా మార్చడం

**NGOల కోసం సిద్ధం చేయబడింది | ఆగస్టు 2026**

### ఈ మార్గదర్శక పరిధి మరియు నిజాయితీ

Monitoring and Evaluation (M&E) అనేది తనకంటూ ప్రత్యేకమైన వృత్తిపరమైన సాహిత్యం కలిగిన ఒక ప్రత్యేక రంగం. ఈ గైడ్ దానిని బోధించడానికి ప్రయత్నించదు. దీని పరిధి మరింత పరిమితమైనది మరియు ఆచరణాత్మకమైనది: భారతీయ NGOలకు nonprofit rates వద్ద అందుబాటులో ఉన్న tools మరియు ఆ tools నిజంగా ఉపయోగకరమైన ఫలితాలను అందిస్తాయా లేదా నిర్ణయించే data practices.

### ⚠ నిర్ధారించలేకపోయిన అంశాలు

NGOలలో విస్తృతంగా ఉపయోగించే కొన్ని ప్రత్యేక M&E platforms — KoboToolbox మరియు Power BI nonprofit pricing సహా — ఈ గైడ్ కోసం పరిశోధన చేసిన సమయంలో వాటి అధికారిక live pages ద్వారా నిర్ధారించలేకపోయాము. ఏదైనా tool యొక్క terms నిర్ధారించబడని చోట, ఈ పత్రం సంఖ్యలను పేర్కొనకుండా విషయాన్ని స్పష్టంగా తెలియజేస్తుంది. ఏ toolను ఎంచుకునే ముందు దాని pricing మరియు eligibilityని నేరుగా provider వద్ద నిర్ధారించండి.

## Toolతో కాదు, ప్రశ్నతో ప్రారంభించండి

NGO data workలో అత్యంత సాధారణ వైఫల్యం తప్పు softwareను ఎంచుకోవడం కాదు. ఏదైనా నిర్దిష్ట ప్రశ్నకు సమాధానం ఇవ్వని భారీ మొత్తంలో dataను సేకరించడం, ఆ తర్వాత funder outcomes గురించి అడిగినప్పుడు నమ్మకంగా ఏమీ చెప్పలేకపోవడం అసలు సమస్య.

ఏ toolను ఎంచుకునే ముందు, మీ సంస్థ నిజంగా సమాధానం ఇవ్వాల్సిన కొన్ని ముఖ్యమైన ప్రశ్నలను రాసుకోండి:

* మేము ఎంతమంది వ్యక్తులను చేరుకున్నాం, ఆ సంఖ్యపై మనకు ఎంత నమ్మకం ఉంది?
* మేము మార్చాలని లక్ష్యంగా పెట్టుకున్న విషయం నిజంగా మారిందా?
* కార్యక్రమంలోని ఏ భాగాలు ఇతర భాగాల కంటే మెరుగ్గా పనిచేస్తున్నాయి, ఎక్కడ?
* ఈ నిర్దిష్ట funderకు ఏమి report చేయాలి, ఏ formatలో, ఎప్పటిలోగా?

మీరు సేకరించే ప్రతి field ఈ ప్రశ్నల్లో కనీసం ఒకదానితో సంబంధం కలిగి ఉండాలి. ఏ ప్రశ్నకూ ఉపయోగపడని fields కేవలం అదనపు ఖర్చు — వాటిని సేకరించడానికి staff time, నిల్వ చేయడానికి storage risk, analysis సమయంలో noise.

### ఒక ముఖ్యమైన సంబంధం

ఇది data protectionతో నేరుగా సంబంధం కలిగి ఉంటుంది. ఒక beneficiary గురించి అవసరం లేని ప్రతి field మీరు రక్షించాల్సిన data మరియు భవిష్యత్తులో leak అయ్యే అవకాశం ఉన్న సమాచారం. తక్కువ dataను సేకరించడం మంచి practice మాత్రమే కాదు, తక్కువ risk కూడా.

## మీరు ప్రాప్యతను నిర్ధారించగల Tools

క్రింది tools వాటి providers యొక్క స్వంత nonprofit pages ద్వారా నిర్ధారించబడ్డాయి:

| Tool                       | Nonprofit Terms                                          | ఉపయోగం                                                                           |
| -------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Microsoft Power Apps       | 10 users వరకు ఉచితం; తరువాత ప్రతి userకు నెలకు $2.50 USD | Custom low-code data collection లేదా case management app నిర్మించడం              |
| Microsoft Power Automate   | ప్రతి userకు నెలకు $3.75 USD, yearly paymentతో           | పునరావృత పనులను automate చేయడం — form responsesను sheetకు పంపడం, reminders పంపడం |
| Google Analytics           | Google for Nonprofitsలో చేర్చబడింది                      | Website మరియు campaign reachను అర్థం చేసుకోవడం                                   |
| Google Cloud / Azure / AWS | Cloud Infrastructure guidesలో పేర్కొన్న credits          | Spreadsheets సరిపోని సమయంలో databaseను host చేయడం                                |
| Microsoft Copilot Studio   | Nonprofit portal ద్వారా అందుబాటులో ఉంది                  | మీ స్వంత dataపై AI agents నిర్మించడం — pricingను తనిఖీ చేయండి, ప్రచురించబడలేదు   |

## పరిశీలించాల్సిన Tools, Terms నిర్ధారించబడలేదు

* **KoboToolbox** — humanitarian మరియు development workలో offline-capable mobile data collection కోసం విస్తృతంగా ఉపయోగిస్తారు. దీని free tier మరియు nonprofit termsను ఇక్కడ నిర్ధారించలేకపోయాము; kobotoolbox.orgలో నేరుగా తనిఖీ చేయండి.
* **Power BI** — Microsoft యొక్క dashboarding tool. పరిశీలించిన Microsoft nonprofit pagesలో ఇది కనిపించలేదు. కాబట్టి Microsoft 365 licensingకు అదనంగా nonprofit pricing ఉందో లేదో తనిఖీ చేయాలి.
* **Looker Studio** — Google యొక్క free dashboard tool, ఇది Google Sheets మరియు Analyticsకు connect అవుతుంది. సాధారణంగా ఉచితంగా ఉపయోగించవచ్చు, అయితే Google for Nonprofits bundleలో దీని inclusion నిర్ధారించబడలేదు.

## Software కంటే ముఖ్యమైన అలవాట్లు

### 1. Data సేకరించే ముందు definitions నిర్ణయించండి

"Beneficiary reached" అంటే ఏమిటి? ఒకసారి కార్యక్రమానికి హాజరైన వ్యక్తినా, లేక programme పూర్తిచేసిన వ్యక్తినా?

సంస్థలు తరచుగా సంవత్సరం మధ్యలో రెండు field teams వేర్వేరు విధాలుగా లెక్కిస్తున్నాయని గుర్తిస్తాయి. దాంతో aggregate data అర్థరహితమవుతుంది. Definitionsను రాసి, అన్ని teamsతో share చేయండి.

### 2. ఒక్కసారి సేకరించండి, అనేకసార్లు ఉపయోగించండి

Field staff internal records కోసం ఒక form, funder కోసం మరో form, annual report కోసం మూడవ form నింపితే data వేర్వేరుగా మారుతుంది మరియు morale కూడా తగ్గుతుంది. ఒక collection processను రూపొందించి, దాని నుంచి వివిధ viewsను తయారు చేయండి.

### 3. Raw dataను analysis నుంచి వేరు చేయండి

Chart తయారు చేయడానికి original recordsను ఎప్పుడూ edit చేయకండి. సేకరించిన raw dataను మార్చకుండా ఉంచి, calculationsను ప్రత్యేక sheet లేదా layerలో చేయండి. ఒక సంవత్సరం తరువాత funder ఏదైనా numberపై ప్రశ్నిస్తే, దాన్ని original record వరకు trace చేయగలగాలి.

### 4. ప్రతిదానికీ timestamp మరియు attribution ఉంచండి

ప్రతి recordలో అది ఎప్పుడు మరియు ఎవరి ద్వారా సేకరించబడిందో ఉండాలి. దీనివల్ల anomaliesను పరిశీలించవచ్చు; మొత్తం datasetను అనుమానించాల్సిన అవసరం ఉండదు.

### 5. Poor connectivity కోసం ప్రణాళిక చేయండి

భారతదేశంలోని అనేక ప్రాంతాల్లో field data collection సమయంలో reliable internet connection ఉంటుందని భావించలేం. Offlineలో పని చేసి తర్వాత sync అయ్యే tools luxury కాదు; connection-dependent toolను ఎంచుకోవడం data కోల్పోయే నిర్ణయం కావచ్చు.

## Reporting: Numbersను అర్థమయ్యేలా చేయడం

ఎవరూ చదవని analysisకు విలువ ఉండదు. కొన్ని సూత్రాలు బాగా పనిచేస్తాయి:

* **Methodologyతో కాదు, findingతో ప్రారంభించండి.** Funders మొదటి lineను చదువుతారు; methodను annexeలో ఉంచవచ్చు.
* **Simple chart typesను ఉపయోగించండి.** వెంటనే అర్థమయ్యే bar chart, explanation అవసరమయ్యే sophisticated visualisation కంటే మెరుగైనది.
* **సమయంతో వచ్చిన మార్పును చూపండి.** ఒక snapshot మాత్రమే impactను నిరూపించడానికి అరుదుగా సరిపోతుంది.
* **Data ఏమి చూపలేదో నిజాయితీగా చెప్పండి.** Data support చేయని certaintyను ప్రకటించే సంస్థల కంటే limitationsను అంగీకరించే సంస్థలను funders ఎక్కువగా విశ్వసిస్తారు.
* **Reporting periods మధ్య consistent format ఉంచండి**, తద్వారా readers పోల్చగలరు.

## సూచించబడిన follow-up article

మీ Knowledge Hubలో తరువాత data visualisationపై article జోడిస్తే, fundersను అనుకోకుండా తప్పుదోవ పట్టించే failure modesను ప్రత్యేకంగా చర్చించడం విలువైనది — truncated axes, చాలా segments ఉన్న pie charts మరియు underlying sample size లేకుండా percentages పేర్కొనడం అత్యంత సాధారణమైనవి.

## Quick Checklist

* ☐ మీ data సమాధానం ఇవ్వాల్సిన నాలుగు లేదా ఐదు ప్రశ్నలను రాయండి
* ☐ వాటిలో ఏ ప్రశ్నకూ ఉపయోగపడని collection fieldsను తొలగించండి
* ☐ అన్ని field teams మధ్య definitionsపై అంగీకరించి వాటిని document చేయండి
* ☐ Power Apps యొక్క 10 users వరకు free tier మీ అవసరాలను తీరుస్తుందో లేదో తనిఖీ చేయండి
* ☐ Offline collection అవసరమైతే KoboToolbox ప్రస్తుత termsను నేరుగా verify చేయండి
* ☐ Raw dataను analysis నుంచి శాశ్వతంగా వేరుగా ఉంచండి
* ☐ ప్రతి recordలో timestamp మరియు collector ఉండేలా చూసుకోండి
* ☐ Fieldwork అవసరమైతే offlineలో పనిచేసే toolsను ఎంచుకోండి

## মাঠপর্যায়ের রেকর্ডকে এমন রিপোর্টে রূপান্তর করা, যা ফান্ডাররা বিশ্বাস করেন

**NGO-দের জন্য প্রস্তুত | আগস্ট 2026**

### এই গাইডের পরিধি ও সততার কথা

Monitoring and Evaluation (M&E) নিজস্ব পেশাগত সাহিত্য ও মানদণ্ডসম্পন্ন একটি পৃথক ক্ষেত্র, এবং এই গাইড সেটি শেখানোর চেষ্টা করে না। এর পরিধি আরও সীমিত ও ব্যবহারিক: ভারতীয় NGO-দের জন্য nonprofit rates-এ উপলব্ধ tools এবং সেই data practices, যা নির্ধারণ করে এই tools থেকে আদৌ কোনো কার্যকর ফল পাওয়া যাবে কি না।

### ⚠ যেসব বিষয় যাচাই করা যায়নি

NGO-দের মধ্যে ব্যাপকভাবে ব্যবহৃত কিছু বিশেষায়িত M&E platform — যার মধ্যে KoboToolbox এবং Power BI-এর nonprofit pricing রয়েছে — এই গাইডের গবেষণার সময় তাদের নিজস্ব live pages থেকে যাচাই করা যায়নি। কোনো tool-এর terms নিশ্চিত না হলে, এই নথি অনুমানভিত্তিক figures দেওয়ার পরিবর্তে তা স্পষ্টভাবে জানায়। কোনো tool ব্যবহারের আগে সরাসরি provider-এর কাছ থেকে pricing এবং eligibility নিশ্চিত করুন।

## Tool দিয়ে নয়, প্রশ্ন দিয়ে শুরু করুন

NGO data work-এর সবচেয়ে সাধারণ ব্যর্থতা ভুল software বেছে নেওয়া নয়। সমস্যা হলো এমন বিপুল পরিমাণ data সংগ্রহ করা যা কোনো নির্দিষ্ট প্রশ্নের উত্তর দেয় না। এরপর কোনো funder যখন outcomes সম্পর্কে জানতে চান, তখন আত্মবিশ্বাসের সঙ্গে কিছু বলা সম্ভব হয় না।

কোনো tool নির্বাচন করার আগে আপনার সংস্থাকে সত্যিই যে কয়েকটি প্রশ্নের উত্তর দিতে হবে, সেগুলো লিখে রাখুন:

* আমরা কতজন মানুষের কাছে পৌঁছেছি এবং সেই সংখ্যাটি নিয়ে আমরা কতটা নিশ্চিত?
* আমরা যে পরিবর্তন ঘটানোর লক্ষ্য নিয়েছিলাম, সেটি কি সত্যিই ঘটেছে?
* Programme-এর কোন অংশগুলো অন্যগুলোর তুলনায় ভালো কাজ করছে এবং কোথায়?
* এই নির্দিষ্ট funder-কে কী report করতে হবে, কোন format-এ এবং কবে?

আপনি যে প্রতিটি field সংগ্রহ করেন, তার সঙ্গে এই প্রশ্নগুলোর অন্তত একটির সম্পর্ক থাকা উচিত। যেসব fields কোনো প্রশ্নের সঙ্গে সম্পর্কিত নয়, সেগুলো শুধুই অতিরিক্ত খরচ — সংগ্রহ করতে staff time, সংরক্ষণ করতে storage risk এবং analysis-এর সময় noise।

### একটি গুরুত্বপূর্ণ সংযোগ

এর সরাসরি সম্পর্ক data protection-এর সঙ্গে। একজন beneficiary সম্পর্কে অপ্রয়োজনীয়ভাবে সংগ্রহ করা প্রতিটি field এমন data যা আপনাকে নিরাপদ রাখতে হবে এবং যা ভবিষ্যতে leak হতে পারে। কম data সংগ্রহ করা ভালো practice এবং কম risk—দুই-ই।

## যেসব Tools-এর Access নিশ্চিত করা যায়

নিম্নলিখিত tools তাদের providers-এর নিজস্ব nonprofit pages থেকে নিশ্চিত করা হয়েছে:

| Tool                       | Nonprofit Terms                                                   | ব্যবহার                                                                       |
| -------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Microsoft Power Apps       | 10 users পর্যন্ত বিনামূল্যে; এরপর প্রতি user প্রতি মাসে $2.50 USD | Custom low-code data collection বা case management app তৈরি                   |
| Microsoft Power Automate   | প্রতি user প্রতি মাসে $3.75 USD, yearly payment-এর ক্ষেত্রে       | পুনরাবৃত্ত কাজ automate করা — form responses sheet-এ পাঠানো, reminders পাঠানো |
| Google Analytics           | Google for Nonprofits-এর সঙ্গে অন্তর্ভুক্ত                        | Website ও campaign reach বোঝা                                                 |
| Google Cloud / Azure / AWS | Cloud Infrastructure guides-এ উল্লেখিত credits                    | Spreadsheets যথেষ্ট না হলে database host করা                                  |
| Microsoft Copilot Studio   | Nonprofit portal-এর মাধ্যমে উপলব্ধ                                | নিজের data-এর ওপর AI agents তৈরি — pricing যাচাই করুন, কারণ প্রকাশিত নয়      |

## যেসব Tools অনুসন্ধানের যোগ্য, কিন্তু Terms নিশ্চিত নয়

* **KoboToolbox** — humanitarian এবং development work-এ offline-capable mobile data collection-এর জন্য ব্যাপকভাবে ব্যবহৃত হয়। এর free tier এবং nonprofit terms এখানে নিশ্চিত করা যায়নি; সরাসরি kobotoolbox.org-এ যাচাই করুন।
* **Power BI** — Microsoft-এর dashboarding tool। পর্যালোচনা করা Microsoft nonprofit pages-এ এটি তালিকাভুক্ত ছিল না। তাই Microsoft 365 licensing-এর বাইরে nonprofit pricing আছে কি না তা যাচাই করতে হবে।
* **Looker Studio** — Google-এর free dashboard tool, যা Google Sheets এবং Analytics-এর সঙ্গে যুক্ত হয়। সাধারণত বিনামূল্যে ব্যবহার করা যায়, তবে Google for Nonprofits bundle-এর অংশ কি না তা নিশ্চিত করা যায়নি।

## Software-এর চেয়ে বেশি গুরুত্বপূর্ণ অভ্যাস

### 1. Data সংগ্রহের আগে Definitions ঠিক করুন

"Beneficiary reached" বলতে কী বোঝায়? যে ব্যক্তি একবার অনুষ্ঠানে অংশ নিয়েছে, নাকি যে programme সম্পূর্ণ করেছে?

অনেক সংস্থা বছরের মাঝামাঝি আবিষ্কার করে যে দুটি field team ভিন্নভাবে গণনা করছে, ফলে aggregate data অর্থহীন হয়ে যায়। Definitions লিখে রাখুন এবং সেগুলো সব দলের সঙ্গে share করুন।

### 2. একবার সংগ্রহ করুন, বহুবার ব্যবহার করুন

Field staff যদি internal records-এর জন্য একটি form, funder-এর জন্য দ্বিতীয়টি এবং annual report-এর জন্য তৃতীয়টি পূরণ করেন, তাহলে data আলাদা হয়ে যাবে এবং morale-ও ক্ষতিগ্রস্ত হবে। একটি collection process তৈরি করুন এবং সেখান থেকে বিভিন্ন views তৈরি করুন।

### 3. Raw data এবং analysis আলাদা রাখুন

Chart তৈরি করার জন্য কখনও original records edit করবেন না। সংগৃহীত raw data অপরিবর্তিত রাখুন এবং calculations আলাদা sheet বা layer-এ করুন। এক বছর পরে কোনো funder কোনো number নিয়ে প্রশ্ন করলে, সেই number-এর উৎস পর্যন্ত trace করতে পারা উচিত।

### 4. সবকিছুর Timestamp এবং Attribution রাখুন

প্রতিটি record-এ কখন এবং কে তা সংগ্রহ করেছে তা থাকা উচিত। এর ফলে anomalies তদন্ত করা সম্ভব হয়, পুরো dataset-কে অবিশ্বাস করার প্রয়োজন হয় না।

### 5. Poor connectivity-এর জন্য পরিকল্পনা করুন

ভারতের অনেক এলাকায় field data collection-এর সময় reliable internet connection ধরে নেওয়া যায় না। Offline-এ কাজ করে পরে sync করতে পারে এমন tools কোনো luxury নয়; connection-dependent tool বেছে নেওয়া data হারানোর ঝুঁকি নেওয়ার সমান।

## Reporting: Numbers-কে বোধগম্য করা

যে analysis কেউ পড়ে না, তার কোনো মূল্য নেই। কয়েকটি নীতি ভালোভাবে কাজ করে:

* **Methodology নয়, finding দিয়ে শুরু করুন।** Funders প্রথম লাইন পড়েন; method annexe-এ রাখা যায়।
* **Simple chart types ব্যবহার করুন।** সঙ্গে সঙ্গে বোঝা যায় এমন bar chart, ব্যাখ্যার প্রয়োজন হয় এমন sophisticated visualisation-এর চেয়ে ভালো।
* **সময়ের সঙ্গে পরিবর্তন দেখান।** একটি snapshot সাধারণত impact দেখানোর জন্য যথেষ্ট নয়।
* **Data কী দেখাতে পারে না সে বিষয়ে সৎ থাকুন।** Data যে certainty সমর্থন করে না তা দাবি করার চেয়ে limitations স্বীকার করা সংস্থাগুলিকে funders বেশি বিশ্বাস করেন।
* **Reporting periods-এর মধ্যে consistent format রাখুন**, যাতে পাঠক তুলনা করতে পারেন।

## প্রস্তাবিত Follow-up Article

## ફીલ્ડ રેકોર્ડ્સને ફંડર્સ વિશ્વાસ કરે એવા અહેવાલોમાં રૂપાંતરિત કરવું

**NGOs માટે તૈયાર | ઓગસ્ટ 2026**

### આ માર્ગદર્શિકાનો વ્યાપ અને પ્રામાણિકતા

Monitoring and Evaluation (M&E) પોતાના વ્યાવસાયિક સાહિત્ય અને ધોરણો ધરાવતું એક અલગ ક્ષેત્ર છે અને આ માર્ગદર્શિકા તેને શીખવવાનો પ્રયાસ કરતી નથી. તેનો વ્યાપ વધુ મર્યાદિત અને વ્યવહારુ છે: ભારતીય NGOs માટે nonprofit rates પર ઉપલબ્ધ tools અને એવી data practices, જે નક્કી કરે છે કે આ tools ખરેખર ઉપયોગી પરિણામ આપે છે કે નહીં.

### ⚠ જે બાબતોની ચકાસણી થઈ શકી નથી

NGOs દ્વારા વ્યાપક રીતે ઉપયોગમાં લેવાતા કેટલાક વિશિષ્ટ M&E platforms — જેમાં KoboToolbox અને Power BIની nonprofit pricingનો સમાવેશ થાય છે — આ માર્ગદર્શિકા માટેના સંશોધન દરમિયાન તેમના પોતાના live pages પરથી ચકાસી શકાયા નથી. જ્યાં કોઈ toolની termsની પુષ્ટિ થઈ નથી, ત્યાં આ દસ્તાવેજ આંકડા જણાવવાને બદલે તે બાબત સ્પષ્ટ કરે છે. કોઈપણ tool પસંદ કરતા પહેલાં તેની pricing અને eligibility સીધી provider પાસેથી ચકાસો.

## Toolથી નહીં, પ્રશ્નથી શરૂઆત કરો

NGO data workમાં સૌથી સામાન્ય નિષ્ફળતા ખોટું software પસંદ કરવું નથી. સમસ્યા એ છે કે કોઈ ચોક્કસ પ્રશ્નનો જવાબ ન આપતો ઘણો બધો data એકત્ર કરવામાં આવે છે અને પછી funder outcomes વિશે પૂછે ત્યારે વિશ્વાસપૂર્વક કંઈ કહી શકાતું નથી.

કોઈપણ tool પસંદ કરતા પહેલાં તમારી સંસ્થાએ ખરેખર જે થોડા મહત્વપૂર્ણ પ્રશ્નોના જવાબ આપવા જોઈએ તે લખી લો:

* અમે કેટલા લોકો સુધી પહોંચ્યા અને આ સંખ્યા અંગે અમને કેટલો વિશ્વાસ છે?
* અમે જે પરિવર્તન લાવવાનું નક્કી કર્યું હતું તે ખરેખર આવ્યું છે?
* Programmeના કયા ભાગો બીજા ભાગો કરતાં વધુ સારી રીતે કાર્ય કરે છે અને ક્યાં?
* આ ચોક્કસ funderને શું report કરવું છે, કયા formatમાં અને ક્યારે સુધીમાં?

તમે એકત્ર કરો તે દરેક fieldનો સંબંધ આમાંથી ઓછામાં ઓછા એક પ્રશ્ન સાથે હોવો જોઈએ. જે fields કોઈ પ્રશ્ન સાથે જોડાયેલા નથી તે માત્ર વધારાનો ખર્ચ છે — તેને એકત્ર કરવા માટે staff time, સંગ્રહ કરવા storage risk અને analysis દરમિયાન noise.

### એક મહત્વપૂર્ણ જોડાણ

આનો સીધો સંબંધ data protection સાથે છે. Beneficiary વિશે અનાવશ્યક રીતે એકત્ર કરાયેલ દરેક field એવું data છે જેને તમારે સુરક્ષિત રાખવું પડશે અને જે ભવિષ્યમાં leak થઈ શકે છે. ઓછો data એકત્ર કરવો એ સારી practice પણ છે અને ઓછું risk પણ.

## Software કરતાં વધુ મહત્વની Habits

### 1. Data એકત્ર કરતા પહેલાં Definitions નક્કી કરો

"Beneficiary reached"નો અર્થ શું છે? જે વ્યક્તિ એક વખત કાર્યક્રમમાં હાજર રહી હોય તે, કે જેણે સંપૂર્ણ programme પૂર્ણ કર્યું હોય તે?

સંસ્થાઓને ઘણીવાર વર્ષના મધ્યમાં ખબર પડે છે કે બે field teams અલગ રીતે ગણતરી કરી રહી છે, જેના કારણે aggregate data અર્થહીન બની જાય છે. Definitions લખી રાખો અને તેને તમામ teams સાથે share કરો.

### 2. એકવાર Collect કરો, અનેકવાર ઉપયોગ કરો

જો field staff internal records માટે એક form, funder માટે બીજું અને annual report માટે ત્રીજું form ભરે, તો data અલગ પડી જશે અને morale પર પણ અસર થશે. એક collection process ડિઝાઇન કરો અને તેમાંથી અલગ અલગ views બનાવો.

### 3. Raw dataને Analysisથી અલગ રાખો

Chart બનાવવા માટે original recordsને ક્યારેય edit ન કરો. એકત્રિત raw dataને અસ્પર્શિત રાખો અને calculations અલગ sheet અથવા layerમાં કરો. એક વર્ષ પછી funder કોઈ number વિશે પ્રશ્ન કરે ત્યારે તેને મૂળ record સુધી trace કરી શકાય તે જરૂરી છે.

### 4. દરેક વસ્તુમાં Timestamp અને Attribution રાખો

દરેક recordમાં તે ક્યારે અને કોના દ્વારા collect કરવામાં આવ્યો હતો તે હોવું જોઈએ. આથી anomaliesની તપાસ કરી શકાય છે, આખા dataset પર અવિશ્વાસ કરવાની જરૂર પડતી નથી.

### 5. Poor connectivity માટે આયોજન કરો

ભારતના ઘણા વિસ્તારોમાં field data collection દરમિયાન reliable connection હોવાની ખાતરી કરી શકાતી નથી. Offline કામ કરીને પછી sync કરી શકતા tools luxury નથી; connection-dependent tool પસંદ કરવું data ગુમાવવાનું જોખમ સ્વીકારવા જેવું છે.

## Reporting: Numbersને સમજવા યોગ્ય બનાવવું

જે analysis કોઈ વાંચતું નથી તેનું કોઈ મૂલ્ય નથી. કેટલીક બાબતો સારી રીતે કામ કરે છે:

* **Methodologyથી નહીં, findingથી શરૂઆત કરો.** Funders પ્રથમ line વાંચે છે; method annexeમાં મૂકી શકાય છે.
* **Simple chart typesનો ઉપયોગ કરો.** તરત સમજાય એવો bar chart, સમજાવવા જરૂરી sophisticated visualisation કરતાં વધુ સારો છે.
* **સમય સાથે થયેલો ફેરફાર બતાવો.** એક snapshot સામાન્ય રીતે impact બતાવવા માટે પૂરતો નથી.
* **Data શું બતાવી શકતું નથી તે અંગે પ્રામાણિક રહો.** Data આધાર ન આપે તેવી certaintyનો દાવો કરતી સંસ્થાઓ કરતાં limitations જણાવતી સંસ્થાઓ પર funders વધુ વિશ્વાસ કરે છે.
* **Reporting periods વચ્ચે consistent format રાખો**, જેથી વાચકો સરખામણી કરી શકે.

## ಫೀಲ್ಡ್ ದಾಖಲೆಗಳನ್ನು ಫಂಡರ್‌ಗಳು ನಂಬುವ ವರದಿಗಳಾಗಿ ಪರಿವರ್ತಿಸುವುದು

**NGOಗಳಿಗಾಗಿ ಸಿದ್ಧಪಡಿಸಲಾಗಿದೆ | ಆಗಸ್ಟ್ 2026**

### ಈ ಮಾರ್ಗದರ್ಶಿಯ ವ್ಯಾಪ್ತಿ ಮತ್ತು ಪ್ರಾಮಾಣಿಕತೆ

Monitoring and Evaluation (M&E) ತನ್ನದೇ ಆದ ವೃತ್ತಿಪರ ಸಾಹಿತ್ಯ ಮತ್ತು ಮಾನದಂಡಗಳನ್ನು ಹೊಂದಿರುವ ಒಂದು ಪ್ರತ್ಯೇಕ ಕ್ಷೇತ್ರವಾಗಿದೆ. ಈ ಮಾರ್ಗದರ್ಶಿಯ ಉದ್ದೇಶ ಅದನ್ನು ಕಲಿಸುವುದಲ್ಲ. ಇದರ ವ್ಯಾಪ್ತಿ ಹೆಚ್ಚು ಸೀಮಿತ ಮತ್ತು ಪ್ರಾಯೋಗಿಕವಾಗಿದೆ: ಭಾರತೀಯ NGOಗಳಿಗೆ nonprofit ratesನಲ್ಲಿ ಲಭ್ಯವಿರುವ tools ಮತ್ತು ಆ toolsಗಳಿಂದ ನಿಜವಾಗಿಯೂ ಉಪಯುಕ್ತ ಫಲಿತಾಂಶ ದೊರೆಯುತ್ತದೆಯೇ ಎಂಬುದನ್ನು ನಿರ್ಧರಿಸುವ data practices.

### ⚠ ಪರಿಶೀಲಿಸಲಾಗದ ವಿಷಯಗಳು

NGOಗಳಲ್ಲಿ ವ್ಯಾಪಕವಾಗಿ ಬಳಸಲಾಗುವ ಕೆಲವು ವಿಶೇಷ M&E platforms — KoboToolbox ಮತ್ತು Power BIಯ nonprofit pricing ಸೇರಿದಂತೆ — ಈ ಮಾರ್ಗದರ್ಶಿಗಾಗಿ ನಡೆಸಿದ ಸಂಶೋಧನೆಯ ಸಮಯದಲ್ಲಿ ಅವುಗಳ ಸ್ವಂತ live pages ಮೂಲಕ ಪರಿಶೀಲಿಸಲಾಗಲಿಲ್ಲ. ಯಾವುದೇ toolನ terms ದೃಢೀಕರಿಸಲಾಗದಿದ್ದಲ್ಲಿ, ಈ ದಾಖಲೆಯು figures ನೀಡುವ ಬದಲು ಅದನ್ನು ಸ್ಪಷ್ಟವಾಗಿ ತಿಳಿಸುತ್ತದೆ. ಯಾವುದೇ tool ಆಯ್ಕೆ ಮಾಡುವ ಮೊದಲು ಅದರ pricing ಮತ್ತು eligibilityಯನ್ನು ನೇರವಾಗಿ providerನಿಂದ ಪರಿಶೀಲಿಸಿ.

## Toolನಿಂದಲ್ಲ, ಪ್ರಶ್ನೆಯಿಂದ ಪ್ರಾರಂಭಿಸಿ

NGO data workನಲ್ಲಿ ಅತ್ಯಂತ ಸಾಮಾನ್ಯ ವೈಫಲ್ಯವೆಂದರೆ ತಪ್ಪಾದ software ಆಯ್ಕೆ ಮಾಡುವುದು ಅಲ್ಲ. ಯಾವುದೇ ನಿರ್ದಿಷ್ಟ ಪ್ರಶ್ನೆಗೆ ಉತ್ತರ ನೀಡದ ದೊಡ್ಡ ಪ್ರಮಾಣದ data ಸಂಗ್ರಹಿಸುವುದೇ ಸಮಸ್ಯೆ. ನಂತರ funder outcomes ಬಗ್ಗೆ ಕೇಳಿದಾಗ ವಿಶ್ವಾಸದಿಂದ ಏನನ್ನೂ ಹೇಳಲು ಸಾಧ್ಯವಾಗುವುದಿಲ್ಲ.

ಯಾವುದೇ tool ಆಯ್ಕೆ ಮಾಡುವ ಮೊದಲು ನಿಮ್ಮ ಸಂಸ್ಥೆಯು ನಿಜವಾಗಿಯೂ ಉತ್ತರಿಸಬೇಕಾದ ಕೆಲವು ಪ್ರಮುಖ ಪ್ರಶ್ನೆಗಳನ್ನು ಬರೆಯಿರಿ:

* ನಾವು ಎಷ್ಟು ಜನರನ್ನು ತಲುಪಿದ್ದೇವೆ ಮತ್ತು ಆ ಸಂಖ್ಯೆಯ ಬಗ್ಗೆ ನಮಗೆ ಎಷ್ಟು ವಿಶ್ವಾಸವಿದೆ?
* ನಾವು ಬದಲಾಯಿಸಲು ಉದ್ದೇಶಿಸಿದ್ದ ವಿಷಯ ನಿಜವಾಗಿಯೂ ಬದಲಾಗಿದೆಯೇ?
* Programmeನ ಯಾವ ಭಾಗಗಳು ಇತರ ಭಾಗಗಳಿಗಿಂತ ಉತ್ತಮವಾಗಿ ಕಾರ್ಯನಿರ್ವಹಿಸುತ್ತಿವೆ ಮತ್ತು ಎಲ್ಲಿ?
* ಈ ನಿರ್ದಿಷ್ಟ funderಗೆ ನಾವು ಏನು report ಮಾಡಬೇಕು, ಯಾವ formatನಲ್ಲಿ ಮತ್ತು ಯಾವಾಗ?

ನೀವು ಸಂಗ್ರಹಿಸುವ ಪ್ರತಿಯೊಂದು field ಕೂಡ ಈ ಪ್ರಶ್ನೆಗಳಲ್ಲಿ ಕನಿಷ್ಠ ಒಂದಕ್ಕೆ ಸಂಬಂಧಿಸಿರಬೇಕು. ಯಾವುದೇ ಪ್ರಶ್ನೆಗೆ ಸಂಬಂಧಿಸದ fields ಕೇವಲ ಹೆಚ್ಚುವರಿ ವೆಚ್ಚ — ಅವುಗಳನ್ನು ಸಂಗ್ರಹಿಸಲು staff time, ಸಂಗ್ರಹಿಸಲು storage risk ಮತ್ತು analysis ಮಾಡುವಾಗ noise.

### ಒಂದು ಪ್ರಮುಖ ಸಂಬಂಧ

ಇದು data protectionಗೆ ನೇರವಾಗಿ ಸಂಬಂಧಿಸಿದೆ. Beneficiary ಬಗ್ಗೆ ಅನಗತ್ಯವಾಗಿ ಸಂಗ್ರಹಿಸಲಾದ ಪ್ರತಿಯೊಂದು field ನೀವು ಸುರಕ್ಷಿತವಾಗಿಡಬೇಕಾದ data ಮತ್ತು ಭವಿಷ್ಯದಲ್ಲಿ leak ಆಗಬಹುದಾದ ಮಾಹಿತಿ. ಕಡಿಮೆ data ಸಂಗ್ರಹಿಸುವುದು ಉತ್ತಮ practice ಕೂಡ ಹೌದು ಮತ್ತು ಕಡಿಮೆ risk ಕೂಡ ಹೌದು.
